root_cause.text: A locking mismatch in KVM/arm64 let kvm_vcpu_init_nested() reallocate and free the shared kvm->arch.nested_mmus array under config_lock instead of mmu_lock, while other paths iterate that array under mmu_lock, causing a use-after-free race.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that "kvm->arch.nested_mmus[] is walked under kvm->mmu_lock" including MMU notifier paths, but "kvm_vcpu_init_nested() reallocates the array and frees the old buffer while holding only kvm->arch.config_lock"; the patch fixes this by allocating separately, then taking write_lock(&kvm->mmu_lock) to copy/swap the array and only kvfree(tmp) after releasing the lock.

intent_record.intent_summary: Safely grow the nested MMU array under mmu_lock by replacing kvrealloc() with allocate-copy-swap logic that preserves and fixes MMU back-pointers.
intent_record.what: The code replaces an unconditional kvrealloc() of kvm->arch.nested_mmus with a conditional growth path that runs only when num_mmus exceeds kvm->arch.nested_mmus_size. In that path, it allocates a new zeroed array with kvcalloc(), takes kvm->mmu_lock for writing, copies existing entries with memcpy(), updates each copied pgt->mmu back-pointer to the new array element, swaps the new array into kvm->arch.nested_mmus, releases the lock, and frees the old array with kvfree(). The old direct kvrealloc()-based reallocation and its post-swap back-pointer fixup logic are removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this avoids in-place or unlocked reallocation of the nested MMU array and instead performs array growth by allocating a separate buffer, updating internal back-pointers before publication, and swapping the pointer under mmu_lock. This makes expansion safer for concurrent access to nested_mmus and its embedded pgt->mmu relationships, while still preserving existing entries and initializing only newly added MMUs afterward.

grouping_result.intent: Safely grow the nested MMU array under mmu_lock by replacing kvrealloc() with allocate-copy-swap logic that preserves and fixes MMU back-pointers.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by changing nested MMU array growth to a safe allocate-copy-swap scheme under mmu_lock, avoiding realloc/free of kvm->arch.nested_mmus while other paths may access it under that lock and preserving required MMU back-pointers.

candidates.rationale: This reallocation can free and replace the shared nested_mmus array while using the wrong lock (config_lock per root cause), racing with readers/writers that access the array under mmu_lock and directly enabling the use-after-free.

This publishes the newly reallocated array pointer after kvrealloc may have moved/freed the old storage, making the lock-domain mismatch visible to concurrent mmu_lock-protected users and contributing to the UAF race.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs reallocation of the shared kvm->arch.nested_mmus array in kvm_vcpu_init_nested() while operating under config_lock rather than mmu_lock. Because kvrealloc() may free the old backing storage and return a new pointer, it creates the core use-after-free race with concurrent paths that access the array under mmu_lock.

This statement publishes the replacement nested_mmus pointer after the unsafe reallocation path. In the presence of the lock mismatch, concurrent mmu_lock-protected users may still be traversing the old array that kvrealloc() could already have freed, so this statement is part of exposing the stale-pointer/UAF condition.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it contains both the allocator/reallocator for `kvm->arch.nested_mmus` and other paths that access the same array under `mmu_lock`, which is exactly the root-cause area. The vulnerable construct is present in `kvm_vcpu_init_nested()`: it performs `tmp = kvrealloc(kvm->arch.nested_mmus, ...);` and later updates `kvm->arch.nested_mmus = tmp;` / `kvm->arch.nested_mmus_size = num_mmus;`, but there is no acquisition of `kvm->mmu_lock` anywhere in this function. The root cause says this reallocation/free must be serialized with `mmu_lock` because other paths iterate the shared array under that lock. This same snippet shows such other paths: `lookup_s2_mmu()` has `lockdep_assert_held_write(&kvm->mmu_lock);` and iterates `for (int i = 0; i < kvm->arch.nested_mmus_size; i++) { struct kvm_s2_mmu *mmu = &kvm->arch.nested_mmus[i]; ... }`. Likewise `get_s2_mmu_nested()` asserts `lockdep_assert_held_write(&vcpu->kvm->mmu_lock);` and accesses `kvm->arch.nested_mmus[...]`. `kvm_vcpu_load_hw_mmu()` also explicitly takes `write_lock(&vcpu->kvm->mmu_lock);` before calling into that path. Therefore this commit introduces exactly the mismatch described: a shared array is reallocated/freed in one path without `mmu_lock`, while other paths access it while holding `mmu_lock`, enabling a use-after-free race if `kvrealloc()` moves/frees the old allocation. There is no visible fix here such as taking `mmu_lock` in `kvm_vcpu_init_nested()` before `kvrealloc()` and publication of the new pointer, so the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant reallocation/error-handling logic inside `kvm_vcpu_init_nested()`, which is sufficient to determine whether the stale-pointer/UAF condition is present. The fix is already present: after successful `krealloc` (`if (!tmp) return -ENOMEM;`), the code immediately does `swap(kvm->arch.nested_mmus, tmp);`. This means `kvm->arch.nested_mmus` is updated to the newly allocated array before any further initialization that may fail. The old array pointer is retained in `tmp` only for comparison/use during back-pointer adjustment. The back-pointer repair also operates on the live array now: `kvm->arch.nested_mmus[i].pgt->mmu = &kvm->arch.nested_mmus[i];`. Newly initialized entries are also initialized via `init_nested_s2_mmu(kvm, &kvm->arch.nested_mmus[i]);`. Critically, on failure, cleanup is performed on `kvm->arch.nested_mmus[i]` and the function returns without restoring the old pointer, matching the commit message's fix strategy of keeping the new allocation installed while leaving `nested_mmus_size` unchanged. Also, the old vulnerable assignment-at-end pattern is gone: the line `kvm->arch.nested_mmus = tmp;` was removed, and only `kvm->arch.nested_mmus_size = num_mmus;` remains on success. Therefore the vulnerable construct (leaving `kvm->arch.nested_mmus` pointing to stale freed memory after failed reallocation/initialization) is absent, and the function already contains the fix.
